observations: Field validation state: `.field.has-error input` gets a red 1.5px border (#ff3b30) plus a red box-shadow, and each `.field-error` message is prefixed with an inline red circle-exclamation SVG — visible on all seven flagged fields in the loading/error screenshots (e.g. 'Enter a valid email address' under Email).

Submission state: `setSubmitting(true)` disables the button (opacity 0.6, cursor not-allowed) and swaps the label to an animated `.spinner` ring (20px, 0.7s rotation) plus 'Processing…', confirmed by the async rater's item 1 evidence.

Order success: a 72px green (#34c759) `.check-circle` containing a white SVG checkmark sits above the 'Order confirmed' heading; failure: the `.alert.error` banner pairs a red warning-icon SVG with the message text on a #fff2f2 background.
Metrics corroborate a graphics-forward page: `desktop.graphical` counts 4 svg + 8 badges = 12 total, against only 54 page words.
Measured `desktop.viewportWords` is 49 and `pageWords` 54 for the whole checkout — the page carries almost no prose at all.
`helperWords: 0` and `longLeafWords: 0`; there is not a single `p`/`small` helper sentence or leaf element over 12 words in the idle DOM.
Button labels: `labels.count: 1`, `meanWords: 2`, `maxWords: 2` ('Pay $127.97'); the only other clickable copy is the two-word 'Try again' retry link — all within the ≤3-word anchor.
Field labels are one to two words each (Email, Full name, Address, City, Postal code, Country, Card number, Expiry, CVC); nothing restates what the UI already shows.
The single non-form line, 'Encrypted and secure' (3 words), is a trust cue rather than narration; error strings like 'Enter your postal code' are one clause with no preamble.
Terminology is consistent end to end: label 'Postal code' ↔ error 'Enter your postal code' ↔ API field `postalCode`; 'Pay $127.97' matches the summary 'Total $127.97' exactly.

Error copy matches behavior: 'Connection lost. Please check your internet and try again.' is accompanied by a working 'Try again' button (async item 6 observed a second submitOrder without reload), and every client message ('Enter a valid email address', 'Enter a valid CVC') corresponds to the actual validation rule in `clientValidate()`.

One issue found: the `.secure-note` claim 'Encrypted and secure' asserts data handling the page does not perform — the submission is a plain `window.api.submitOrder` call with no encryption of its own, so this is an unbacked trust claim in a transactional UI.
Placeholders are legitimate format examples, not filler: 'you@example.com', '1234 5678 9012 3456', 'MM / YY', '123'.

Interaction detail is clearly checkout-driven: the card input auto-groups digits into 4-blocks, expiry auto-inserts ' / ' after two digits, CVC strips non-digits, and all three carry `inputmode="numeric"`, `maxlength`, and correct `autocomplete` cc-* tokens.

The primary button label 'Pay $127.97' embeds the live order total, and the sticky (`position: sticky; top: 24px`) Order summary keeps items, Subtotal $119.97, Shipping $8.00, and Total $127.97 alongside the form; on mobile `order: -1` moves the summary above the form.

The visual identity is stock: Inter on #f5f5f7 with white 12px-radius cards and the Apple system palette (#0071e3 blue, #ff3b30 red, #34c759 green, #1d1d1f/#6e6e73 grays), a meaningless three-line blue logo, and emoji product thumbnails (☕ 🥬 🧵) — the shop itself has no name or character.
Net: strong task-specific mechanics over a template-grade skin — above 'competent but template-like' but short of a design clearly owned by this shop.

Answered from the idle desktop screenshot alone: purpose read immediately as an online-shop checkout ('Checkout' title, numbered ① Contact ② Shipping ③ Payment cards, Order summary with three priced items) — correct per the brief.

What needs attention read correctly as step ① Contact's empty Email field ('you@example.com' placeholder) at the top of an explicitly numbered sequence, with the bold 'Total $127.97' as the secondary anchor.

The primary action failed the 'obvious' bar: no Pay/submit button is visible anywhere in the 1440×900 idle viewport — it had to be inferred from the step numbering, and metrics confirm the actual primary action is the below-the-fold 'Pay $127.97' button.
Two of three answers correct and obvious, the third correct but only by inference, so 4 rather than 5.
